title: Geysers earthquakes per unit of injected water fell by one third in an early-2014 step that injection, production and well location do not explain (CalGEM wells, ComCat M 2+, 1985-2026)
abstract: We tested if monthly geothermal operations predict later earthquake rates. We summed the CalGEM GeoSteam monthly records of 796 wells at The Geysers and 247 wells at the Salton Sea, and counted USGS ComCat earthquakes within 2 km of the wells. At The Geysers, 15 linear injection and production models fitted on years to 2014 predicted 1.35 to 1.64 times the 2,273 M 2.0+ events of 2015-01 to 2026-07. The observed count was below every bootstrap draw. Declustered, M 1.7+ and M 2.5+ counts gave the same result. With operations as covariates, the rate fell in a step at 2014-02 (range 2014-01 to 2014-03) to 0.64 (0.58-0.70) of the model rate. A step fitted better than a trend by 34 AIC units. Cell models with the new injection locations predicted 283-310 events per year against 194 observed. A cumulative-injection exhaustion term was not supported. A strong production effect fitted on 2004-2014 explained 2015-2026 but predicted 2.1 times the 1987-2003 count. The step was largest for events at 1.5 km depth or less (factor 0.44). Matched NCSN and LBNL magnitudes did not change at the step, and the LBNL catalogue also fell in 2014. Events per Mt injected were 8.7 in 1998-2013, 6.0 in 2014-2025 and about 6.5 in 2024-2026. At the Salton Sea, operations had no positive link in 1990-2012, and declustered 2013-2026 counts were 0.62-0.72 of model forecasts. Limitations: the cause is not identified; injection temperature is missing after 2007; NCSN depths and post-2015 magnitudes are not independently checked; Coso data were empty.
